  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening lines of the maamar for the second day of Sukkos 5731.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The second day of the festival of Sukkos,</t>
    <t s="2">5731</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This maamar is a discourse delivered without prior preparation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(A discourse delivered without prior preparation)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains the difficulty in the verse "Praise Hashem, all nations," questioning why gentiles should praise for the kindness done to Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Praise Hashem, all nations; extol Him, all peoples! For His kindness has overwhelmed us, and the truth of Hashem is forever, Halleluyah."</t>
    <t s="1">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">what is the reason of "for His kindness has overwhelmed us," that because of this the nations and peoples will praise and extol Him?</t>
    <t s="3">And as the Gemara in Pesachim asks,</t>
    <t s="4">"The nations of the world, what is their involvement?"</t>
    <t s="5">Now, Rashi explains</t>
    <t s="6">(in the resolution of the Gemara there),</t>
    <t s="7">that even though His kindness has overwhelmed us,</t>
    <t s="8">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="9">since this is in a revelation that they also see it</t>
    <t s="10">("that they saw what He did for me"),</t>
    <t s="11">therefore they must praise and extol.</t>
    <t s="12">However, this is not sufficient, as it is written in the maamar "Hallelu es Hashem" by our master the Alter Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="13">that "this is not a sufficient reason."</t>
    <t s="14">For from this language it implies that "for His kindness has overwhelmed us" is a reason for "Praise Hashem, all nations," etc.</t>
    <t s="15">(from which it implies that he explains it like the above explanation of Rashi),</t>
    <t s="16">except that it is not a sufficient reason.</t>
    <t s="17">And therefore the Rashbam explains there that "for His kindness has overwhelmed us" is a matter in itself,</t>
    <t s="18">and here it explains that all the more so the nations and peoples must praise and extol for the mighty deeds and wonders that He performed in the world,</t>
    <t s="19">and all the more so we, for His kindness has overwhelmed us more than any other nation and tongue.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
